tools.description:
Create the default store and its _shared/report-format note. Call it when
another tool reports that no store exists.

Idempotent. path must be the current working directory, the directory in
SWARMNOTES_DIR, or the project directory whose .swarmnotes is
SWARMNOTES_DIR. Any other path is an error. Returns root (the store path)
and report_format (its note id).
tools.name: relatum_init

tools.description:
List notes as id, kind, summary, and status. Use it before grep or asking:
after a context refresh, list your scope to find your handoff note; before
using another agent's code, list its scope for an api note.

scope is a directory under the store (e.g. m5/editor); empty lists everything. kind filters
to one of decision, constraint, convention, context, format, finding,
attempt. Superseded notes are omitted unless include_superseded is true.
tag filters to one slug. The store is .swarmnotes/ or $SWARMNOTES_DIR.

limit.description: Return at most this many notes. When notes are left out, the result has more (how many).
limit.title: Limit

since.description: Only notes written or changed at or after this time: a date such as 2026-11-05 (from local midnight, the calendar updated uses) or a time such as 2026-11-05T14:30:00Z or 2026-11-05T14:30:00+11:00 (no zone means local). Pass a modified value from an earlier details listing to see what is new.
since.title: Since

details.description: Also return author, updated, and modified (file time, UTC) per note.
details.title: Details

tools.name: relatum_ls

tools.description:
Fetch one or more notes by ID: the notes a brief lists under Read first,
your handoff after a context refresh, or another agent's api note before
you call its code. Follows superseded_by, including multi-hop chains.

Returns notes (the live note, with chain: the ids followed) and errors (ids
that failed). Other ids are still returned when one id is missing.
include_superseded adds the bodies of the notes each live note replaced.

include_superseded.description: Also return superseded: the notes each live note replaced (id, superseded_by, summary, body), oldest first. For handoffs written as deltas.
include_superseded.title: Include Superseded

tools.name: relatum_get

tools.description:
Create a note. Write one for any fact more than one agent needs, so briefs
and reports cite its id instead of pasting it: a handoff before your context
runs out or your work ends (state, open items, gotchas), an api note when
other agents will call your code, a finding or attempt from your work.

Fails if the id already exists; never overwrites. To replace a note, write
the new one, then call relatum_supersede. kind is decision, constraint,
convention, context, format, finding, or attempt. summary is one line, at
most 200 characters. body is the fact (keep it under ~300 words). tags is
a list of slugs.

summary.description: One line, at most 200 characters; shown in listings.
summary.title: Summary

tools.name: relatum_new

tools.description:
Correct a note in place: replace its summary, body, or tags; updated becomes today.

For small fixes to a note you wrote (author must match the note's author).
To replace a note, or to change one someone else wrote, write a new note and
call relatum_supersede with old set to this note. Superseded notes cannot be edited.

author.description: Who is editing; must be the note's author.
author.title: Author

summary.description: New one-line summary, at most 200 characters.
summary.title: Summary

body.description: New body; replaces the whole body.
body.title: Body

tags.description: New tag slugs; [] removes the tags.
tags.title: Tags

tools.name: relatum_edit

tools.description:
Mark old as replaced by new, e.g. a fresh handoff or api note replacing the
last one. Write new with relatum_new first; it must exist and resolve to a live note.

Later relatum_get calls on old follow the chain (include_superseded also returns
old's body). relatum_ls hides old unless include_superseded is true.
tools.name: relatum_supersede

tools.description:
Lint every note in the store. Run it after editing note files by hand or
before committing .swarmnotes/.

ok is false when there are errors. warnings (long bodies, missing author
or updated) do not fail the check. errors and warnings are the same
strings the CLI prints.
tools.name: relatum_check
